Configure_TC02.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Interface page 3)  Click LAN (X0) Configure button to pop up Edit Interface - X0 windows 4)  Select Undefined or Static from IP Assignment pulldown list 5)  Click OK button to save this setting without errors 6)  Check if the Transparent Mode is unset on LAN (X0) interface from Network/Interface page 7)  Repeat Step 3) to Step 7) above to unset Transparent Mode for other Interfaces defined in LAN, DMZ or custome zone
Configure_TC02.title: User Interface: Configuration - Unsetting Transparent mode
Configure_TC02.result: All steps in Test Excution section above are passed without errors.

Configure_TC03.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Address Object page 3)  Click the Configure button of the LAN (X0) transparent range created in TC-1 (Test Case 1) above to pop up Edit Address Object windows 4)  Change this range to different range out of WAN subnet 5)  Click OK button to save changes 6)  The step above is denied with an error message  Error: Transparent Range not in WAN subnet  is displayed 7)  Change this range to include WAN IP 8)  Click OK button to save changes 9)  The step above is denied with an error message  Error: Transparent Range includes WAN IP  is displayed 10)  Change this range to include WAN Gateway 11)  Click OK button to save changes 12)  The step above is denied with an error message  Error: Transparent Range includes WAN Gateway  is displayed 13)  Change this range to a valid range within WAN subnet 14)  Click OK button to save changes 15)  The step above is accepted
Configure_TC03.title: User Interface: Configuration - Modifying an address object attached to interface

Configure_TC05.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Address Object page 3)  Click Add button for Address Object to pop up Edit Address Object windows 4)  Fill up a name called as DMZ transparent range and an IP address out of WAN subnet for Host 5)  Check to make sure DMZ transparent range is not displayed in a pulldown list of Transparent Range
Configure_TC05.title: Error: Configuration - Invalid IP
Configure_TC05.result: An IP address object out of WAN subnet should not be displayed in a pulldown list of Transparent Range when defining an interface in Transparent mode.

Configure_TC06.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Address Object page 3)  Click Add button for Address Object to pop up Edit Address Object windows 4)  Fill up a name called as DMZ transparent range and an IP range address out of WAN subnet for Host 5)  Check to make sure DMZ transparent range is not displayed in a pulldown list of Transparent Range
Configure_TC06.title: Error: Configuration - Invalid IP range
Configure_TC06.result: An IP range object out of WAN subnet should not be displayed in a pulldown list of Transparent Range when defining an interface in Transparent mode.

Configure_TC08.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Address Object page 3)  Create two address range objects as Range 1 10.0.30.206  10.0.30.207 and Range 2 10.0.30.207  10.0.30.208 and 10.0.30.207 is the overlaped IP address 4)  Use Range 1 as a Transparent range for X0 in Transparent mode 5)  Click X2 Configure button to pop up Edit X2 windows 6)  Select DMZ for Zone and Transparent Mode for IP Assignment 7)  Select Range 2 for Transparent Range 8)  Click OK button to save the changes 9)  An error message  Error: Transparent Range overlaps with other configured Transparent Interface  is displayed to force user to select an address range object not overlapped with Range 1 for Transparent Range
Configure_TC08.title: Error: Configuration - Range overlap
Configure_TC08.result: An error message will be displayed to let user has to select or create a Transparent range not overlapped with other configured Transparent Interface.

Configure_TC09.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Address Object page 3)  Click Del ect button for an address object or an address group object attached to an interface as a Transparent Range 4)  An error message Error: View List for delecting an address object or  Error: Object is in use by Transparent Mode interface  for deleting an address group object is displayed in Status line at the buttom of this page 5)  Click View List for deleting an address abject to pop up an error message windows to see  Object is in use by Transparent Mode interface  is displayed
Configure_TC09.title: Error: Configuration - Deleting an Address object or an Address Group object attached to an interface
Configure_TC09.result: An error message will be displayed to deny this action.

Configure_TC11.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Interface page 3)  Configure an interface in Transparent mode with a Transparent range 10.0.30.206  10.0.30.209 4)  Select an IP address for a host connected on this interface with the following one at a time to access management interface and Internet from this host to chech the result: 10.0.30.205 (out of lower boundary in Transparent range) 10.0.30.206 (same as lower boundary in Transparent range) 10.0.30.207 or 10.0.30.208 (within the Transparent range) 10.0.30.209 (same as higher boundary in Transparent range) 10.0.30.210 (out of higner boundary in Transparent range)

Zones_TC13.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Interface page 3)  Configure an interface (LAN Zone) in Transparent mode 4)  Make sure it is functional.
Zones_TC13.title: Function: Zone and Interface - LAN zone
Zones_TC13.result: The interface within LAN, DMZ or Custom zone (Trusted or Public) is able to be configured in Transparent mode.

Interface_TC16.steps: 1)  Login to management interface through a web browser 2)  Go to Network/Interface page 3)  Configure an interface in Transparent mode 4)  Click Configure button of this interface to pop up Edit windows 5)  Check the checkboxes of ping, HTTP ans HTTPS under management and User Login sections 6)  Make sure this interface is able to be ping or managed by administrator or user through HTTP or HTTPS
Interface_TC16.title: Function: Interface Rules - Management and ping
Interface_TC16.result: An interface in Transparent mode is able to be ping or managed through HTTP or HTTPS only when the related checkbox is checked, otherwise, it should fail.

ARP_TC17.title: Function: ARP Behavior - Transparent to/from WAN
ARP_TC17.result: All ARP items designed for this test must be valid.

Policy_TC22.steps: 1)  Locate two web servers named as Server1 and Server2 connected on X0 (LAN) and X1 (WAN) correspondingly 2)  Create an address object named as Server1 in Network/Address Object page 3)  Add a firewall rule (WAN -> LAN) with HTTP service and destination Server1 from Firewall/Access Rule page 4)  Access the web server (Server1) or (Server2) from a host on WAN or a host on LAN using HTTP to check the result 5)  Repeat this test with the different services such as ping, FTP and Telnet from inbound or outbound direction to check the results
Policy_TC22.title: Function: Connectivity and Policy Rules - Transparent to/from WAN
Policy_TC22.result: All kinds of traffic with different directions defined in policy rules must go through for Transparent to/from WAN.

Group_Func_TC01.steps:
1.Create an address group includes some hosts or ranges which in WAN subnet
2.Config LAN interface X3 transparent to X1, use the AO group in step1
3.Check Network-> Routing page, all auto-added routes are created for the address group, include each AO host or AO range
4.PC connect X3 which config IP as one of the AO group, traffic can pass through
Group_Func_TC01.title: [Func]Verify the auto-added routes are created for transparent mode address group(DTS ID: 203323)
Group_Func_TC01.result: The auto-added routes are created for transparent mode address group

DHCP_TC33.steps: 1)  Connect a host to the interface in Transparent mode 2)  Open a DOS box of this host 3)  Get, release or renew a DHCP IP address using the related DOS commands 4)  Access the management interface or Internet after a DHCP lease is got or renewed
DHCP_TC33.title: Function: DHCP Server for the interfaces in Transparent mode
DHCP_TC33.result: A DHCP lease a host gets are correct and it is able to access management interface and Internet.

TSR_TC35.steps: 1)  Configure X0 or other interfaces defined in LAN, DMZ or custom zone to Transparent mode 2)  Open the TSR from System/Diagnostics page 3)  Compare all transparent mode items with the real transparent mode settings
TSR_TC35.title: Function: Log - TSR

Perf_TC38.steps: 1)  Configure X0 or other interfaces defined in LAN, DMZ or custom zone to Transparent mode 2)  Export a preference file from System/Settings page 3)  Change this interface to NAT mode 4)  Import the preference file just saved with Transparent mode settings
Perf_TC38.title: Function: Perference support - Import and export
Perf_TC38.result: Check the settings after the box restarts to make sure the settings are matched with the previous transparent mode settings.
